hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: US diesel hits an all-time high as refining sets the price
brief.h: The national average reached $5.820 a gallon, edging past the June 2022 record, with the diesel crack spread printing an all-time $108.02 a barrel intraday, East Coast distillate stocks at a record-low 19.3 million barrels - and a hot August payroll print pushing the Fed's rescue further out of reach.
brief.t: The important thing here is what is NOT scarce. Brent is around $96 and off its highs; crude is available. What is not available is the capacity to turn crude into distillate - diesel, heating oil and jet fuel - and that is fixed kit on multi-year build cycles, so it cannot be surged the way a Gulf producer opens a valve. Three wars are pulling on the same narrow pipe at once: roughly 900,000 barrels a day of diesel and 350,000 of jet normally leave the Gulf through a contested strait, Ukraine's drone campaign has hit Russian refineries hard enough that Moscow banned diesel exports through 30 September, and US refiners are running with stretched turnaround intervals. Diesel is the input to freight, farming and heating rather than a consumer choice, which is how a chokepoint eight thousand miles away arrives as a grocery bill. And it is why today's payroll surprise matters more than usual - 162,000 jobs against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1% hardens a Federal Reserve already arguing about a RISE, in an inflation that monetary policy cannot refine.
brief.context: R0, date the rail: this is a late chapter of E1, the 1973-79 epoch that yoked oil to the dollar, crossed with the refining rationalization that followed it - from the early 1980s the rich world stopped building refineries and optimized the ones it kept for light sweet crude and gasoline, while the marginal barrel got heavier, sourer and further away. The desk that decides is neither OPEC nor the Fed; it is the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, with a Russian export ministry as a swing operator nobody appointed. The mechanism is the crack spread - the margin between a barrel of crude and the fuel refined out of it - and when that margin sets records while crude does not, the binding constraint is conversion, not geology. Base rate, and it is the discipline here: outage-driven product-crack spikes mean-revert inside three to six months, and the May 2022 diesel spike was back under $45 by that August, whereas spikes caused by permanent closures persist for years. This one has both causes running, which is why the answer is a probability rather than a call. Influence map: the principal is whoever books record refining margins, the operator is a maintenance schedule, the market is the ULSD futures curve, and the target is a trucking, farming and heating-oil customer with no seat at any of it. Falsifier, dated and now scored: a daily settle below $45 on the US diesel crack before 15 December kills the regime read - that is GEO-026, opened today at 35%.

consp.claim: That the diesel squeeze is engineered rather than incidental - that American refining capacity has been allowed to decay through deferred maintenance and regulatory attrition until a shortage became inevitable, and that the US is exporting fuel out of a shortage it tells its own citizens to endure.
consp.spread: A steady genre on alternative-health and dissident-macro sites since early August. NaturalNews and Newstarget ran near-identical pieces on 3 August headlined that the diesel shortage is real and refineries are at risk of blowing up from lack of scheduled maintenance; Larry C. Johnson's America's Diesel Paradox - a shortage it is supplying, not suffering - circulated on Unz and from there into X energy threads.
consp.read: Two different claims are riding together and they deserve different verdicts. The deferred-maintenance kernel is checkable and partly right: turnaround intervals have stretched, unplanned outages are elevated, and US distillate exports do run near record levels while East Coast stocks sit at 19.3 million barrels - so supplying a shortage describes real cargo flows. The engineered-scarcity leap is the part with no rail: the refinery closures are decades old and driven by margin and complexity economics that predate every actor named. This is downstream of a genuine grievance - the people paying $5.82 have no representation on anyone's maintenance calendar.

angles.effect: book record conversion margins - $108.02 a barrel intraday is the highest ever printed on this spread
gains an external cause for an inflation number it does not control, and fresh leverage to press allies on Hormuz escorting
its refinery campaign is working exactly as designed, which is why blaming it for Western fuel prices is an attempt to disarm a weapon by pricing it
pay the entire bill, with the autumn harvest and the heating season both still ahead of them

dec.kill: If the crack collapses below $45 while Hormuz stays shut, the strait was never the binding constraint and the Russian ban plus refinery outages were. That one observable separates the two stories.

brief.head: Israel declares its south Lebanon security zone complete
brief.h: Defence minister Israel Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge marks the completion of securing control in the security zone in southern Lebanon, and that Israel will not withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country.
brief.t: Read the condition, not the map. Disarmed throughout Lebanon is not a military objective with a completion criterion; it is a political outcome the Lebanese state has never once been able to deliver, and hanging a withdrawal on it converts an operation into an open-ended presence by definition rather than by decision. Israel held a self-declared security zone in south Lebanon from 1985 to 2000 on almost identical logic, withdrew unilaterally when the attrition became domestically unaffordable, and is now rebuilding it on the same ground. The constraint on Netanyahu and Katz is not ideology but a calendar - an election on 27 October and a standing promise that Galilee residents can go home - which makes a declared, mapped, held line the cheapest deliverable on the shelf.
brief.context: R0: the rail predates this headline by four decades. The 1985 security zone was the residue of the 1982 invasion, run through a proxy militia, and its unravelling in May 2000 is the founding legend of Hezbollah's claim to have beaten a conventional army. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground is a manpower expense an air campaign is not. The mechanism is that a held buffer converts episodic war into chronic contact - and the historical record cuts AGAINST alarm here, since fifteen years of the old zone produced roughly two multi-week campaigns, Accountability in 1993 and Grapes of Wrath in 1996, amid continuous low-grade attrition. That is a class base rate near 13% a year against the 32% this book was carrying, which is why an escalation-shaped headline produced a CUT on GEO-004 rather than a raise. Fortna's finding is what keeps the number above the historical rate rather than at it: ceasefires with an agreed third-party verifier hold materially better, and this framework has none while the party being disarmed rejects the premise. The second-order loser is the Lebanese state, asked to disarm a party it does not control while losing the territory that would give it standing to try. Falsifier: an announced withdrawal timetable, or a Lebanese Army deployment onto the ridge under a published mechanism, before 31 December.

consp.claim: That the security zone is a water grab - that the real object of a permanent Israeli line in the south is the Litani river, and that the disarmament condition is a placeholder for annexation.
consp.spread: An old and durable frame that resurfaces every time the line moves. It ran hard across pro-Palestinian X and Reddit threads alongside the Katz statement this week, usually paired with quotations from the 1919 Zionist Organization submission to the Paris peace conference asking for a northern boundary reaching the Litani.
consp.read: The historical kernel is real: the 1919 submission did ask for that boundary, and water has been an Israeli strategic interest in the Levant since the 1950s National Water Carrier disputes. The checkable part fails on geography - the Ali al-Taher ridge sits near Nabatieh and the declared zone is a few kilometres of high ground, not the Litani basin's water infrastructure. What the frame gets right is the durability problem: once a line is held for a condition nobody can satisfy, arguments about its purpose become unfalsifiable, which is precisely why we published a dated withdrawal falsifier instead of a motive.

brief.head: Witkoff and Kushner set to fly to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend
brief.h: TASS reports the two US envoys travelling on 5-6 September to restart talks stalled since February, with Peskov declining to confirm, Moscow reportedly resisting the Kyiv leg, and nobody committing to pause strikes while the envoys are in the air.
brief.t: The informative detail is the objection, not the trip. Russia is reported to be trying to reshape the itinerary so the envoys do not continue to Kyiv - which tells you Moscow values the EXCLUSIVITY of the channel more than it values the meeting, and that is a bargaining position rather than a peace position. Putin said this week that the two are always welcome and that contacts with Kyiv continue through intelligence channels; his own spokesman had called the process a deep pause with no proposals six days before that. Both statements can be true at once, because a live channel with no convergence is the normal condition of a war whose belligerents still price victory differently. The thing to watch this weekend is not whether the planes land but whether anyone tables a ceasefire-in-place text.
brief.context: R0: the epoch is the post-1991 European security settlement whose enforcement mechanism was never written down, and the rail is the Witkoff-Dmitriev channel opened in 2025, which produced the 28-point draft widely read in Kyiv as a demand for surrender. The desk that decides is not the envoy: it is the Russian General Staff's assessment of what another winter of Donbas advance is worth against sanctions attrition, and opposite it a Ukrainian presidency that cannot sign territorial language and survive politically. Reiter's framework is the anchor - wars end when the two sides' expectations about the outcome converge - and shuttle diplomacy is a symptom of that convergence, never a cause of it. The base rate is the discipline: envoy shuttles without an agreed ceasefire text convert into a durable ceasefire at low single-digit rates inside ninety days, which is why today bought GEO-005 exactly two points, to 17%. Influence map: principal Putin, agent the General Staff, narrator TASS, operator the strike tempo over Kyiv this weekend, market the European gas curve, target a Ukrainian grid entering its fourth war winter. Dated falsifier: if no US envoy has landed in either capital by 14 September, this goes back to 14%.

consp.claim: That the negotiation is a business transaction in diplomatic clothes - that Witkoff's real-estate interests and Kushner's Gulf-funded investment vehicle, and their Florida meetings with Kirill Dmitriev of Russia's sovereign wealth fund, mean the terms are being drafted around post-war deal flow rather than around Ukraine.
consp.spread: Loud and bipartisan since the 28-point plan leaked last November - Ukrainian and European commentary, US foreign-policy X, and r/UkrainianConflict all run a version of it whenever a trip is announced.
consp.read: Reported facts do most of the work: Dmitriev runs the Russian Direct Investment Fund, the Florida meetings and repeated Moscow trips are on the record, and the November draft did impose terms widely described as capitulation. The unproven leap is intent - that deal flow is the OBJECTIVE rather than a foreseeable by-product of using private-sector envoys, which is a recurring American practice with a long and mixed record. The boring alternative fits the evidence equally well: a president who trusts two people, dislikes interagency process, and gets the diplomacy that staffing choice produces.

brief.head: Trump declines to say the US would back Britain over the Falklands
brief.h: Asked by a British broadcaster whether Washington would come to Britain's aid in another Falklands conflict, Trump did not answer - and Milei used it within hours to say Argentina must recover the islands and to announce penalties aimed at the Sea Lion oil project.
brief.t: Nobody is invading anything, and that is the wrong thing to watch. Since 1982 the United States has been formally neutral on sovereignty while recognising Britain's administration - and materially helpful to London when it mattered. What Trump withheld today was not a defence commitment; it was the ASSUMPTION of one, and that assumption is what used to make Argentine commercial pressure pointless. Milei is not threatening a landing. He is threatening the shareholders, directors and suppliers of Sea Lion, an offshore project about 220 kilometres north of the islands co-developed by Britain's Rockhopper and Israel's Navitas that has been struggling toward a final investment decision since 2015. Sovereignty claims do not move oil projects. Financing conditions do.
brief.context: R0: the rail is the 1982 settlement, and the deeper epoch is the hemispheric-defence arrangement in which American ambiguity was always the price Britain paid for American help. What predates this headline is not a plot but a relationship - the US-Argentina currency and energy alignment built through 2025-26, in which Milei is Washington's most reliable ideological partner in South America and Vaca Muerta is the hemisphere's largest non-US shale resource. The desk that decides is the State Department's Western Hemisphere bureau and its formal language on sovereignty, not a president answering a hypothetical, and the honest incompetence alternative is named first: Trump answers all hypotheticals expansively, nothing changes at State, and this is a news cycle. The base rate strongly favours that boring read - sovereignty transfers of inhabited territory against the inhabitants' expressed wishes essentially do not happen in the post-1945 order outside decolonization or war, and the 2013 referendum ran 99.8% for remaining British. So forecast the CLASS actually available: commercial, financing and insurance friction on a marginal offshore project, not a South Atlantic war. That is GEO-027, opened today at 12% and resolving on a document rather than an interview.

consp.claim: That a grand bargain is on the table - American diplomatic backing for Argentine sovereignty over the Falklands in exchange for long-term US control of Vaca Muerta, sold as a way to break Chinese and Iranian energy leverage.
consp.spread: Published rather than whispered: the Washington Examiner ran it as an op-ed arguing Trump can crush Iran and China by trading British islands for Argentine oil, and it propagated through X foreign-policy accounts and r/geopolitics within a day of Trump's remarks.
consp.read: This is the most checkable claim on today's board, because it maps exactly onto a frame this desk already tracks - coercive leverage converted into sovereign equity, the pattern visible in the Venezuelan oil venture. The kernel is a real asymmetry: Argentina needs dollars and Vaca Muerta needs capital. The overreach is treating an op-ed as a policy. What would make it more than commentary is a document either way - a published US statement changing the sovereignty language, or an Argentine energy concession with a US federal entity on the cap table.

angles.effect: gets a sovereignty rally that costs nothing and crowds out an economy still in adjustment
gets leverage over London and Buenos Aires simultaneously, from a sentence he can walk back for free
pays in deterrence credibility - No 10 had to reassert that support is unwavering, which is what a guarantee looks like once it has to be restated
carry the real cost, in financing and insurance terms on a project that has never cleared a final investment decision

dec.kill: A published State Department reformulation of the neutrality language, or a Rockhopper or Navitas filing citing Argentine measures as a reason for delay - either converts this from a news cycle into a policy.

brief.head: Kenya orders Tata Chemicals out after 115 years at Lake Magadi
brief.h: Ruto told the Indian company to pack up and leave for exporting raw soda ash instead of processing it into glass and chemicals locally, and said two new companies will take over the operation in Kajiado.
brief.t: This is the second African government in two days to make domestic processing a condition of extraction - Ghana required gold refined at home before export on Wednesday, Kenya expelled a soda-ash miner on Thursday - and the pair is the story rather than either one alone. The argument behind it is a hundred years old and has a name: Prebisch and Singer's claim that raw-commodity exporters face slowly deteriorating terms of trade against manufactured goods, so the only escape is to capture the processing step. The working modern template is Indonesia, which banned nickel ore exports, genuinely did build a domestic smelting industry, and lost a WTO case in 2022 for doing it. The question for Magadi is whether soda ash is scarce enough to make anyone build the glass plant - because Wyoming trona dominates world soda-ash trade, and a buyer who cannot get Kenyan ore simply buys American.
brief.context: R0: the epoch is the post-colonial terms-of-trade rail, running from the 1950s Prebisch-Singer thesis through the 1970s New International Economic Order to today's export bans, and the concession itself predates Kenyan independence - Magadi has been mined since 1911. The desk that decides is not the presidency but whoever underwrites the two replacement companies, and that is where the boring explanation lives: opposition figures, including DCP secretary-general Senator John Methu, have said publicly that this is about private gain rather than industrial policy, and naming two unnamed successors to a 115-year concession is the classic patronage tell. The mechanism to watch is scarcity, not sovereignty - an export ban builds an industry only where the resource is genuinely hard to substitute, and soda ash is not, which makes a rent transfer more likely than an industrialization. Base rate: resource-nationalization episodes since 1960 recover pre-nationalization output within five years in only a minority of cases, and almost never where the state must also attract fresh capital under an expropriation shadow. Falsifier, and it is clean: if Magadi exports resume at 80% or more of 2025 volumes within twelve months under a new operator with no glass plant financed, this was a rent transfer; a funded, under-construction glass or chemicals plant in Kajiado by mid-2027 scores the industrial-policy read.

consp.claim: That the expulsion is not about value addition at all - that the two unnamed replacement companies are already spoken for by people close to the presidency, and that a century-old concession is being transferred rather than reformed.
consp.spread: Made on the record by Kenyan politicians rather than anonymously: allies of former deputy president Rigathi Gachagua, led by DCP secretary-general Senator John Methu, accused Ruto of frustrating the Tata investors for alleged personal monetary gain, and the claim ran hard on Kenyan X and in Daily Nation comment threads within a day.
consp.read: This is the incompetence-or-patronage alternative the house rules require us to name, and here it is not merely an alternative - it is the leading hypothesis until the successors are named. The checkable observable is public and cheap: publish the two companies, their beneficial owners, and the tender under which they were selected. A government doing genuine industrial policy has no reason to withhold that; one doing a transfer has every reason.

angles.effect: a resource-nationalism win delivered in person, in a county with a long-standing and genuine grievance
acquire a 115-year asset with no published tender - the largest single transfer of value in the announcement
carry the write-down, and every other foreign operator in Kenya reprices its political risk on the same day

angles.party: Magadi workers and the soda-ash market
angles.effect: workers face an operator transition with no guaranteed continuity; the world market barely notices, because Wyoming trona sets the price

dec.kill: Publication of the two successor companies with beneficial ownership and a competitive tender document would move this from patronage toward policy. Continued silence past thirty days is itself an answer.

watch: The weekly EIA distillate print. East Coast stocks below 19.3 million barrels would set a new record low into the heating season; a US diesel crack settling under $45 before 15 December scores GEO-026 and kills our regime read. Those two numbers matter more than any statement about oil this month

Whether a US envoy plane actually lands in Moscow or Kyiv by 14 September - and, far more important, whether anyone tables a ceasefire-in-place text. A trip is not a term sheet, and this is our own dated falsifier on GEO-005

Whether the State Department restates or reformulates the 1982 Falklands neutrality language, and whether Rockhopper or Navitas files anything citing Argentine measures as a reason for delay. One is the policy; the other is the transmission

Whether Kenya publishes the two successor companies at Magadi with beneficial ownership and a tender document. Thirty days of silence is itself the answer, and it decides whether Wednesday's Ghana rule and Thursday's Kenya expulsion are an industrial-policy class or a patronage class

Whether Seoul's cabinet sends a Hormuz consent motion to the National Assembly at all, after today's walk-back. The presidential office now says these were general descriptions of options and nothing has been decided - our own card last night was a step ahead of that, and this is the observable that settles it
lesson: Today's mechanism is eighty years old and it explains the diesel price better than any headline about tankers. In 1945 the economist Albert Hirschman published National Power and the Structure of Foreign Trade, and his argument was deceptively simple: the power one country holds over another is not measured by how much trade flows between them, but by how HARD it would be for the weaker side to replace it. Volume is not leverage. Substitutability is leverage. Apply that to oil and the whole story flips. Crude is highly substitutable - there are dozens of producers, and a barrel from Guyana burns much like a barrel from Basra - which is why the crude price is around $96 and calm-ish while the world's most important strait is contested. Refining capacity is NOT substitutable, because you cannot buy a distillation and hydrocracking unit off a shelf, and that is why the margin for turning crude into diesel just printed an all-time record of $108 a barrel while crude did not. Hirschman's prediction, restated for today, is that political power is quietly migrating to whoever controls the least substitutable step in the chain - which right now is not the oilfield but the refinery, and increasingly a refinery in India, the Gulf or China rather than in the West. It also predicts the behaviour we are watching: Russia banning diesel exports, Ukraine bombing refineries rather than wells, and Washington leaning on allies about a strait, are all the same move made from different seats - each side reaching for the bottleneck rather than the volume. Handle the theory honestly: Hirschman was writing about interwar German trade policy and his index has real limits, chiefly that it assumes states can perceive their own dependence, which they routinely cannot until the bill lands. But the test is scoreable and it is on our board as GEO-026 - if the diesel crack falls back under $45 before mid-December, the bottleneck was temporary and the leverage was borrowed; if it does not, the West has discovered a dependency it had not priced.

quiz.q: Crude is around $96 and off its highs, but the diesel refining margin just printed an all-time record of $108 a barrel. What does that combination actually tell you?
options: That there is less oil in the ground than the market believed
That the binding shortage is in refining capacity, not in crude - and refineries take years to build, so the constraint cannot be surged away
That speculators have cornered the diesel market
That OPEC has secretly cut production
quiz.why: A crack spread is the margin between a barrel of crude and the fuel refined out of it. When that margin sets records while the crude price does not, the scarce thing is the kit, not the geology - and that distinction is the whole story, because valves open in hours and refineries take years.

quiz.q: Katz said Israel will not leave southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon. Why did the brief treat that sentence as the important one?
options: Because it is a threat to invade Beirut
Because it means Israel will withdraw within months
Because it violates the ceasefire text
Because it is a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to deliver, which turns a withdrawal into something that happens by decision rather than by completion
quiz.why: Watch the exit criterion, not the map. A condition no one can satisfy is not a milestone - it is an open-ended presence with a milestone's grammar, which is exactly how the 1985-2000 security zone worked.

quiz.q: The brief CUT the odds of an Israel-Hezbollah multi-week campaign on the day Israel declared a permanent security zone. What was the reasoning?
options: Because a held buffer historically produces chronic low-grade attrition instead of episodic campaigns - the 1985-2000 zone produced about two multi-week operations in fifteen years
Because Hezbollah has been destroyed
Because the ceasefire now has a third-party verifier
Because Israel's election makes any operation impossible
quiz.why: That base rate is roughly 13% a year for the escalation class, well below the 32% the book was carrying - and publishing a cut on an escalatory-sounding day is the test of whether a forecast follows evidence or mood.

quiz.q: Russia is reported to be trying to stop the US envoys continuing from Moscow to Kyiv. What does that behaviour most likely reveal?
options: That Russia is close to accepting a ceasefire
That Russia does not want to negotiate at all
That Moscow values exclusive access to the channel more than it values the meeting - a bargaining position rather than a peace position
That the envoys are working for Ukraine
quiz.why: Wanting the conversation to itself is a strong tell about intent. A party genuinely seeking convergence wants both sides in the room; a party seeking terms wants to speak to the guarantor alone.

quiz.q: CRITICAL THINKING. A widely shared claim says the diesel shortage is engineered - that US refineries were deliberately allowed to decay until scarcity was inevitable, and that America is exporting fuel out of a shortage. Which observable would most usefully test it?
options: Whether pundits on TV admit refining is a problem
Whether diesel prices go higher next month
Whether the government denies the claim
Whether the timeline of refinery closures predates the actors being blamed, and whether closure decisions track margins and complexity economics rather than any policy date
quiz.why: The checkable half of the claim is real - export flows and stretched maintenance intervals are documented. The engineered half needs a rail older than the crisis, and refinery closures driven by margin economics over four decades do not supply one. Testing a claim means finding the part that could fail, not the part that feels true.

plumbing.read: Today the physical leg and the monetary leg pointed the same way for the first time this week, and that is what makes it worth writing down. The physical print: US diesel at a record $5.820 a gallon, the crack at an all-time $108.02 intraday, East Coast distillate at a record-low 19.3 million barrels, August national stocks the thinnest since 1982. The monetary print: 162,000 August payrolls against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, into a Federal Reserve whose live debate is a rate RISE rather than a cut, and Waller leaning to hold only if inflation keeps improving. That combination is the manual's RESCUE WITHHELD class - a market certain the firemen are coming, in a shock the firemen cannot fix, because a policy rate does not build a hydrocracker. The long end has already priced it: ten-year 4.79%, thirty-year 5.27%, both above our published red lines, with the reverse-repo buffer at $0.70bn and effectively gone. What is STILL not printing is the milkshake tape - the broad dollar is 118.75 and soft on the month, so this remains a term-premium and supply-shock event rather than a dollar squeeze, and we say so rather than reaching for the more dramatic reading. Falsifier, dated: a diesel crack back under $45 before 15 December with the strait still contested marks this an outage, not a regime, and scores GEO-026 against us.
plumbing.epoch: E1 reopened - the 1973-79 oil-yoked-to-the-dollar rail, running now through its refining sequel rather than its crude one - alongside E6, whose September-2019 repo confession never closed (Fed still buying bills, ON RRP at $0.70bn), and E7, the weaponized-settlement rail opened by the 2022 reserve freeze and visible today in a Russian export ban and an Argentine sanctions decree aimed at a British-Israeli oil project.
